St. Louis, Mo.-East St. Louis, Ill.
In defining the commercial zone of St. Louis, Mo., and East St. Louis, Ill., in St. Louis, Mo.-East St. Louis, Ill., Commercial Zone, 1 M.C.C. 656 (1937), the commercial zone exemption was removed with respect to transportation to and from Belleville, Ill., which is contiguous to East St. Louis. In the Interim Report, we stated our belief that the policy considerations requiring the partial removal of the exemption as to Belleville no longer exist. We stated that we believe that Belleville and East St. Louis form a single tecminal, that movements between the two points are local in nature and not a line-haul or over-the-road movement, and that the exemption as to Belleville should be restored. This proposal is strongly supported by many shippers located in Belleville, and we adopt it in this final report. Restoration of the exemption to Belleville will permit shippers located there the same flexibility of service that their competitors located in adjacent and nearby communities within the zone now enjoy. It also will allow us to dispose of the present complicated zone description and to define the St. Louis-East St. Louis commercial zone pursuant to the populationmileage formula.
Several interested parties object to defining the St. Louis-East St. Louis, commercial zone by application of the proposed population-mileage formula. They urge that an industrial area of western St. Louis County, Mo., which is not embraced by the proposed formula, be included in the zone.
